string.text: GP-25 «Koster» Underbarrel Grenade Launcher

A single-shot, muzzle-loading underbarrel grenade launcher designed for assault rifles of the Warsaw Pact nations. It features a double-action trigger mechanism with a manual safety and an automatic firing lock if installed improperly.\n \n%c[0,1,255,255]•%c[default] Ammunition: VOG-25, VOG-25P
M203 Underbarrel Grenade Launcher

A variant of the single-shot M203 grenade launcher featuring a 3-inch shortened barrel and a Picatinny rail mounting interface. Thanks to this versatile mount, the model has seen widespread adoption across the globe.
 
 %c[0,1,255,255]•%c[default] Ammunition: M209 grenade (40 mm)
M203 Underbarrel Grenade Launcher with DeltaPoint PRO

A shortened modification of the single-shot 40mm M203 grenade launcher, adapted for mounting on a Picatinny rail.
The main feature of this version is a compact DeltaPoint Pro red dot sight pre-installed on a side quadrant mount. This engineering solution allows the shooter to engage targets with rapid and accurate indirect fire without relying on cumbersome mechanical leaf sights.

AG36 Underbarrel Grenade Launcher

A high-tech German 40mm underbarrel grenade launcher developed by Heckler & Koch. Unlike the M203 series, the breech of the AG36 swings outward to the side when reloading, allowing the operator to use non-standard, longer munitions. The module is equipped with its own ergonomic pistol grip, significantly improving handling during firing.
 
 %c[d_purple] • %c[ui_gray_2] Ammunition: %c[ui_gray_1]M209 grenade (40 mm)
M320A1 Underbarrel Grenade Launcher

A modern 40mm underbarrel grenade launcher system derived from the German AG36 and adopted by the US Army to replace the aging M203.
Retaining the key advantage of its predecessor—a side-opening barrel for loading specialized long munitions—the launcher module is noticeably more compact and features a folding foregrip for improved ergonomics.
 
 %c[0,1,255,255] • %c[default] Ammunition: M209 grenade (40 mm)
GP-5 Grenade Launcher Module

A grenade launcher module designed for integration with the OTs-14 «Groza» rifle-grenade system. Based on the GP-25 underbarrel grenade launcher, its design includes several modifications, most notably a single unified trigger used for firing both grenades and standard rifle ammunition. Due to its unique mounting mechanism, this module cannot be fitted onto other weapon platforms.\n \n%c[0,1,255,255]•%c[default] Ammunition: VOG-25, VOG-25P
RGD-5 Hand Grenade

The RGD-5 (Hand Grenade, Distance - GRAU index 57-G-717) is a Soviet offensive hand grenade developed in the early 1950s to replace the aging RG-42. The casing consists of upper and lower thin stamped steel hemispheres containing a 110-gram TNT bursting charge. It is used with standardized UZRGM or UZRGM-2 fuzes. Thanks to its thin-walled construction, the body shatters upon detonation into small, fast-decelerating fragments, minimizing the risk to the thrower and allowing it to be used during a running assault.

F-1 Hand Grenade

The F-1 (GRAU index 57-G-721), colloquially known as the "Limonka" (Lemon), is a Soviet defensive hand grenade designed to eliminate enemy manpower in defensive operations. Derived from the French F1 model 1915 grenade, its key feature is a heavy cast-iron body with deep external grooves, packed with 60 grams of TNT. Upon detonation, the iron body shatters into heavy, lethal shrapnel capable of inflicting casualties at distances up to 200 meters. Due to its massive fragmentation radius, throwing this grenade is strictly permitted only from behind solid cover, inside an APC, or from a trench.

M84 Flashbang Grenade

The M84 is a stun grenade currently issued to the United States Armed Forces and SWAT units across the nation. Upon detonation, it emits an extremely loud 170–180 decibel bang and a blinding flash exceeding one million candela within a 5-foot (1.5-meter) radius. This is sufficient to induce immediate temporary blindness, deafness, tinnitus, and inner ear disturbance. Exposed personnel suffer from severe disorientation, confusion, and loss of coordination. The M84 is loaded with a magnesium-based pyrotechnic charge inside a thin aluminum sub-canister, enclosed by a cast-steel perforated body. Unlike high explosives used in conventional ordnance, the pyrotechnic charge produces a subsonic deflagration rather than a supersonic detonation, minimizing overpressure blast damage.

«Zarya-2» Hand Grenade

The «Zarya-2» flashbang hand grenade features a spherical plastic body filled with a pyrotechnic compound based on fulminate of mercury and magnesium powder. The body consists of upper and lower hemispheres. The top hemisphere holds an external tube with a friction-pull ignition fuse, sealed with a corrugated rubber cap for waterproofing. The lower hemisphere is fitted with a spiked rubber cover to reduce the chance of structural breakage upon impact with hard obstacles. Casing diameter without cover: 56 mm.

M67 hand grenade

The M67 is an American offensive-defensive hand grenade adopted by the United States in 1968 to replace the M26. Due to its characteristic spherical shape, it earned the nickname «baseball». The 64 mm diameter steel body is notched on the inside with a special matrix to form fragments and contains 184 grams of Composition B explosive (a mixture of TNT and RDX). Upon detonation, the body shatters into approximately 710 small fragments. Used with the M201A1 fuze, ensuring safe throwing in both open spaces and enclosed structures.

RDG-2 Smoke Hand Grenade

The RDG-2 is a Soviet smoke hand grenade designed for deploying short-term tactical smoke screens, blinding enemy firing positions, signaling, and marking helicopter landing zones. It utilizes a cylindrical compressed cardboard casing filled with a specialized anthracene or metal-chloride smoke mixture. Once the match-head striker fuse is activated, the mixture burns intensely without open flame, outputting a thick, dense cloud of greyish-white or black smoke (depending on variant). The heavy screen effectively conceals movement across open terrain and degrades enemy aiming visibility.

An incendiary hand grenade (thermite grenade) that generates intense heat upon ignition (reaching up to 2200 degrees Celsius) through a violent thermite reaction, where powdered aluminum reacts with iron oxide to produce a stream of molten iron and aluminum oxide. Filled with 600 to 800 grams of thermite mixture.

A modified Soviet offensive hand grenade, re-engineered to throw sharp fragments of electrical-type artifacts instead of standard shrapnel—making it a terror to inhabitants of the Zone. It is designed to clear fast-moving mutant packs such as snorks, blind dogs, pseudodogs, and boars. Rumor has it that a well-placed throw can even bring down a helicopter. Features a wide casualty radius. Find cover before throwing!

VOG-17 «Khattapka»

An improvised fragmentation hand grenade, known among stalkers as the «khattapka». It is field-crafted from a 30mm VOG-17 round meant for the AGS-17 automatic grenade launcher. Since the original impact fuze will not arm when thrown by hand, it is carefully unscrewed and replaced with a standard UZRGM series hand grenade fuze using an adapter or electrical tape. Thanks to a notched steel coil ribbon inside the casing, detonation of the RDX filler produces a dense cloud of razor-sharp fragments, surpassing the lethal effect of a standard RGD-5.

A powerful RDX bursting charge delivers strong high-explosive impact, while the pre-scored casing jacket scatters shrapnel effectively across enemy cover.

RGN Hand Grenade

The RGN (Hand Grenade Offensive, GRAU index 7G21) is a Soviet offensive grenade developed in the late 1970s to replace the RGD-5. Its primary technical feature is a unique impact sensor combined with a dual-mode impact/delay UDZ fuze. When thrown, the grenade detonates instantly upon striking any hard surface (ground, wall, rocks, trees), leaving targets no time to dive for cover. If no impact occurs, a pyrotechnic self-destruct timer detonates the charge after 3.2–4.2 seconds. The spherical body composed of two aluminum alloy hemispheres features internal scoring for controlled fragmentation into small slivers that lose velocity rapidly, ensuring safe deployment for the user in open ground.

RGO Hand Grenade

The RGO (Hand Grenade Defensive, GRAU index 7G22) is a Soviet defensive grenade developed alongside the RGN to replace the older F-1. Like its offensive counterpart, it is equipped with an advanced UDZ impact-delay fuze that detonates instantly on contact with obstacles, eliminating any delay an enemy could exploit to take cover. The primary difference is the heavy spherical body composed of four steel sub-hemispheres. Both inner and outer surfaces feature deep cross-hatch scoring, generating over seven hundred lethal fragments upon detonation. Must be thrown strictly from behind solid shelter.

Stielhandgranate Model 1924

The Stielhandgranate Model 1924 was a stick hand grenade manufactured and used by Nazi Germany from 1924 until the end of World War II. The grenade is activated by pulling a cord attached to a friction igniter through the fuze assembly. Many of these grenades made their way into the Zone from vast WWII military stockpiles. They are favored by less-equipped factions due to ease of throwing compared to conventional grenades, though some combatants complain about the overall length and fuze delay before detonation.

M24 Bundle Grenade

This anti-tank bundle grenade is a formidable explosive device engineered specifically to defeat armored vehicles and fortifications. Consisting of additional explosive heads lashed around a central stick grenade, it delivers a concentrated blast upon detonation. Thanks to its specialized design and high-explosive filler paired with a heavy casing, it poses a severe threat to armored targets. Deploying it requires precise timing and tactical bravery, often forcing soldiers to approach in close proximity to enemy armor. Renowned for its ability to disable and destroy tanks, this improvised anti-tank charge is a critical anti-armor tool for infantry units on the battlefield.

Stielhandgranate Model 1924 - Splitterring

The Splitterringgranate is an explosive weapon with significant historical heritage that saw widespread combat during major conflicts. Built to maximize destruction, this hand grenade features a segmented fragmentation sleeve slipped over the warhead. When detonated, it unleashes a dense shower of deadly shrapnel in all directions, inflicting heavy casualties and shattering enemy personnel. Combining tremendous explosive force with lethal close-quarters performance, the Splitterring stick grenade remains an iconic symbol of infantry warfare.
